:::{#cor-cross-entropy-entropy}
#### Entropy is the cross-entropy of a distribution with itself

Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with [probability mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) $p$ on $\set{1, \ldots, K}$.
Then

$$H(p, p) = \entropyf{X}.$$

:::

::: proof

By @thm-cross-entropy-expectation with $q = p$, $H(p, p) = \E{-\log p_X}$.
Since $\P(X = k) = p_k$, the random variable $-\log p_X$ is the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) $\surprisalf{X}$,
so $H(p, p) = \E{\surprisalf{X}} = \entropyf{X}$ by the definition of [entropy](#def-entropy).

:::

::: {#rem-cross-entropy-expected-surprisal}
#### Cross-entropy is an expected surprisal

By @thm-cross-entropy-expectation, the cross-entropy $H(p, q)$ is the average [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of outcomes drawn from $p$,
with each surprisal measured by $q$ as $-\log q_k$.
By @cor-cross-entropy-entropy, measuring with $p$ itself gives the entropy.

:::
